captions.text: Alaya Pulse: live polls, quizzes and tests for your presentations
Here’s how to run your first session, step by step
Step 1: build your deck. Click Import to bring in your slides
Use a PDF or HTML file. From PowerPoint or Google Slides? Save it as a PDF first
An HTML file is cut into separate slides for you
Wrong number of slides? You can fix it yourself
Open the file, find the last slide number, and type it in
Now every slide is separate, so you can add questions in between
Add a question anywhere in your deck
Pick a type: multiple choice, word cloud, open-ended, rating or ranking
Type your question, then the answers
The preview beside it shows how it looks on the big screen
Add a timer to make it a race: faster answers score more
Pick a colour or a gradient. The text colour is set for you
Already have lots of questions? Add them all at once
Download the template. Ask ChatGPT or Gemini to fill it in from your Word document
Upload the file, then choose where they go: live questions, a test or a survey
Each question becomes its own slide
Slide Overview shows your whole deck
Drag a slide to move it
Made a mistake? Use Undo and Redo
Click Save to keep your deck
Tick the right answer, and quiz scoring turns on by itself
Right answers score points. Faster answers score more
A leaderboard is added to the end of your deck for you
Step 2: present. Click Start Show
Your audience scans the QR code with their phone camera. No app or sign-up needed
This is what your audience sees on their phone
They’re in. Questions will appear on their phone
Press the arrow keys to move between slides
Or move your mouse to the edge of the screen for arrow buttons
Tip: for HTML slides, use these arrows, not the arrows inside your slides
On a question slide, answers come in live
When you’re ready, show the results
Want to ask again? Reset the votes so everyone can answer again
The timer starts again too
Want everyone to answer a set of questions at their own pace, like an exam?
Add a Self-paced test. The questions inside the gold box are the test
Import your test questions, or add them one by one
The right answers are already marked, so the test scores itself
Set one time limit for the whole test
Choose when people see their score, and what happens after the test
And pick a colour or gradient for the big screen
A self-paced test starts with the rules, while people get ready
Press Start test. The clock starts for everyone
Everyone gets all the questions on their own phone
Some questions have more than one right answer
Tap any number to go back to a question
Some questions want a written answer
Check your answers, then submit
Done! Your score shows when the test ends
See live who is still answering and who has finished
You can add time, pause, or end the test early
Then the leaderboard. Most right answers wins. If it’s a tie, the faster finish wins
Everyone sees their place and the right answers
Then go through the answers together, one question at a time
For written answers, everyone’s answers fill the screen first
Show your marking guide when you’re ready, or skip it
Want feedback? Add a survey. It works like a Google Form inside your deck
Questions inside the pink frame are the survey. Give it a title
Import the questions, or add them one by one
Each question can be Must answer or Optional
It’s anonymous, unless you choose Ask for names
It stays open until you close it, so people can answer after the show too
The survey opens on everyone’s phone. Anyone else can scan the code
Watch the responses come in
Everyone gets all the questions at once
Some let you tick more than one
Sent. That’s it
Show results steps through each question
The survey link keeps working after the show, until you close it
Finished? Press Esc, then End session
Type who it was with, so you can find this session later
Step 3: afterwards, open Results
Each session shows its name, so groups are easy to tell apart
Tabs switch between the live questions, the test and the survey
Survey answers come as charts, ready to print, or as Word, Excel or an AI summary
Download everything as Excel or PDF
Share gives you a link, so colleagues can use your deck
